text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming/generate (dedicated pool: pool-7). Auto-page sent to oncall.

ben_oncall: seeing it. p99 jumped to ~3.8s last 5m (baseline 0.9s). streaming stalls reported. paging now. @shayla_sre you on?

shayla_sre: on. adding context: queue depth for pool-7 spiked to 1.2k, warmup backlog accumulating. autoscaler shows delayed slot readiness ~120s due to warmup handshake.

ajay_platform: adding logs from autoscaler: 
```
[autoscaler] scale_event: requested 8 slots -> acked 8
[handshake] slot_ready: false (warmup_pending)
[warmup] init_gpu: 30s, load_model: 70s, kv_rehydrate: 20s
[handshake] total_warmup=120s
```

maria_prodeng: customer impact: CS flagged high-error/timeout rate from AcmePayments and CheckoutCo on streaming endpoints. CS says multiple timeouts within a user session. @cs_lead please confirm severity.

cs_lead: confirmed. AcmePayments on premium dedicated plan. They saw partial transcript gaps and reconnects. They've escalated to CSM. No broad data loss but degraded UX. They've asked for ETA.

ben_oncall: immediate mitigation idea: 1) temporarily divert new streaming sessions for these customers to hosted pools (lower latency) 2) apply per-tenant soft rate-limit to reduce queue growth 3) kick warmup preloads for models in pool-7 manually. Thoughts?

shayla_sre: agree. host fallback is safest for customer impact. Two caveats: hosted pools have lower reserved capacity for large bursts; need token routing change for those tenants. I can push routing override if ok.

ajay_platform: I can run a targeted routing override. Command I will use: 
```
POST /internal/routing/override
{"tenant": "acmepayments", "target": "hosted-us-east", "duration": 1800}
```
Will instrument and rollback after stabilization.

ben_oncall: do it. add CheckoutCo as well. Keep duration 30m then reassess.

ajay_platform: launched override for AcmePayments and CheckoutCo -> hosted-us-east. now seeing queue depth drop ~12% in pool-7 already.

shayla_sre: deploying short-term soft rate-limit: 20% throttling on new sessions for non-enterprise tenants on pool-7. This should preserve warmup slots for prioritized tenants. Pushing policy now.

maria_prodeng: heads-up to CSM: routing override in place for AcmePayments and CheckoutCo; they might see requests from a different endpoint. This should reduce timeouts.

ben_oncall: also pushing warmup preloads. Procedure: for each model shard on pool-7 run warmup sequence: curl local warmup endpoint; prewarm kv cache. Example: 
```
for id in $(cat pool7-models.txt); do curl -X POST http://pool-7.local:9090/warmup -d '{"model": "$id", "prompt": "<warmup>"}'; done
```
Doing now in background.

shayla_sre: I'm watching the warmup jobs. A few nodes failing to apply quantization kernels — looks like a kernel cache miss triggering fallback to CPU which elongates init. I can restart the runtime to force recompile on the node. Planning to restart 2 failing nodes sequentially to avoid further disruption.

ajay_platform: pairing with you on node restarts. I'll take node-7a then node-7b. I'll cordon and drain before restart. Estimated downtime per node ~90s.

ben_oncall: coordinate and callouts: 1) @ajay_platform cordon+restart nodes 2) @shayla_sre continue warmup preloads & monitor KV rehydrate 3) I'll message CS + CSM with updates 4) escalate to infra if restarts don't fix kernel mismatch.

incident-bot: NOTE: oncall handoff scheduled in 40m to night oncall. Current incident severity: SEV2.

maria_prodeng: CSM responded: AcmePayments reported reduced reconnects after routing override. They still see occasional 2s pauses but nothing like before. Thanks.

shayla_sre: after node restarts and preloads p99 dropped to ~1.1s, p95 ~0.45s. Streaming stalls reduced; KV miss rate is trending down. Queue depth now 230 (was 1.2k).

ben_oncall: nice. keep watching for 15m. Any config changes causing this?

ajay_platform: found a misconfigured autoscaler policy for pool-7: warmup_delay_ms was set to 100000 (100s) instead of 10000 (10s) due to a bad rollout from yesterday. That caused handshake backoff to be too aggressive. Rolling back the policy now.

shayla_sre: that matches observed behavior. Autoscaler still requested slots but handshake waited too long before trying warmup. Fixing policy should prevent recurrence. Opening a postmortem ticket.

ben_oncall: assign follow-ups: - ajay_platform to roll back autoscaler policy permanently and add unit test (owner: ajay) - eng-runtime (shayla) to add diagnostic that alerts on kernel cache miss spikes (owner: shayla) - product/ops (maria) to coordinate customer debriefs (owner: maria)

maria_prodeng: creating follow-up ticket and CSM blurb. We should offer credit to AcmePayments given degraded UX.

cs_lead: agreed. drafting CSM note.

incident-bot: UPDATE: p99 back under SLO threshold for 10m. Monitoring continues.

ben_oncall: moving to monitoring state. I'm leaving a runbook note: root cause = autoscaler warmup_delay misconfiguration + kernel cache miss on two nodes -> cascade delay in slot readiness -> queue amplification -> p99 SLO breach for streaming endpoints. Mitigations executed: tenant routing override, soft rate-limits, manual warmup, node restarts, autoscaler rollback.

shayla_sre: note for postmortem: add timeline, include warmup init waterfall, ensure autoscaler policy validation in CI, and add customer impact summary.

ajay_platform: logging actions and config diffs to the incident ticket now.

ben_oncall: thanks all. I'll hand this over at the scheduled oncall rotation but keep pagerduty followups enabled until postmortem closes.

maria_prodeng: CSM confirms AcmePayments requests a short incident summary + mitigation steps. I'll send within 2 hours.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: status -> monitoring. closing page.

ben_oncall: closing thread here. If anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:
